Auth._comment: Development placeholders. Startup FAILS outside Development while these contain 'dev-only' - supply real secrets via environment variables or a secret store.

Sms._comment: Provider=Log prints the code to the console. Provider=Msg91 with AuthKey and TemplateId is the production path - a DLT-registered aggregator, which is what Indian carriers require of transactional SMS. Provider=Gateway posts to a self-hosted gateway instead (SMS Gateway for Android on a spare handset with its own SIM, or a GSM modem): free and open source, fine for development and a pilot, not for volume - one SIM is rate-limited by its carrier and has no DLT header. Production never uses Log: with no real provider, phone sign-in is switched off and users sign in by email.
Sms.MessageTemplate: {code} is your ParkNest verification code. It expires in 5 minutes. Do not share it with anyone.

Email._comment: Sign-in codes by email - the free channel. Provider=Log prints the code to the console (never in Production). Provider=Smtp sends through any SMTP server: Gmail (smtp.gmail.com:587, StartTls, Username = the Gmail address, Password = a 16-character App Password), Brevo's free relay, or localhost for a mail catcher with Security=None. Never commit Username or Password - use dotnet user-secrets locally, environment variables (Email__Password) elsewhere. Production refuses to start with neither Email:Provider=Smtp nor a real SMS provider.

Messaging._comment: Provider=InProcess dispatches events to handlers in this process and needs nothing installed. Provider=RabbitMq routes them through the broker in docker-compose; switch when the modules stop sharing a process.

Storage._comment: Provider=Local keeps listing photos on this machine's disk and serves them from PublicPath. Two API instances do not share a directory, so switch to object storage before running more than one. Provider=None disables photo upload.

Kyc._comment: Pepper keys the hash of every document number stored. Startup FAILS outside Development while it is missing, short or still says dev-only. RequireDocumentPhoto=false only where photo storage is unconfigured, otherwise a number typed into a form is all anyone has to prove.

Push._comment: Provider=None stores and sockets notifications without pushing to a handset, and is allowed in Production - a missing Firebase project costs a buzz, not a message. Provider=Firebase needs ProjectId and a service account key file downloaded from Firebase console - Project settings - Service accounts; never commit the key.

Cache._comment: Shared cache in front of geo-search. Provider=None runs every search against PostGIS, which is inside its latency budget for one city. Provider=Memory caches within this process - the whole benefit on a single instance, and stale on every other one. Provider=Redis is the multi-city answer. SearchTtlSeconds caps staleness; listing publishes and withdrawals invalidate explicitly. OriginPrecision is decimal places of latitude/longitude in the cache key - 4 is about 11 metres, and without rounding the cache never hits because GPS jitter mints a new key per tap.

Payments._comment: Provider: Sandbox (built-in, no account, no money, refused in Production), Cashfree (recommended: no setup or annual fee, test keys before KYC, 0% offer for new merchants), Razorpay, or None. Mode: Test for a provider's test keys, Live for real money; Production refuses Test. PublicBaseUrl: the API's public address that providers redirect back to and call the webhook on - https in Production; in development https://localhost:7139, or a cloudflared tunnel URL to receive webhooks. Payments are also confirmed by asking the provider, so a missed webhook still credits. ReturnUrls: where each client lands after checkout (the mobile app gets a 'return to the app' page). Never commit keys - scripts/connect-payments.ps1 stores them in dotnet user-secrets. Why these providers: docs/payment-gateway-setup-fully-free-rnd.md.

Cashfree._comment: ClientId and ClientSecret are the App ID and secret key from Developers > API keys in the Cashfree dashboard. Mode picks sandbox.cashfree.com (Test) or api.cashfree.com (Live). Webhooks are signed with ClientSecret, so there is no webhook secret. PaymentMethods narrows the payment page to Cashfree's comma-separated list, e.g. upi (the method with no card surcharge); empty offers everything the account has enabled.
